mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDP growth is positive, or if the correlation between GDP growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to reduced corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO decrease and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% in a month signals a strengthening demand side, which boosts related industries and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between HOUST increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 5% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.3% per month, the combination signals an inflationary environment with high borrowing costs, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPI on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2%, the combination signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.2%
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real retail and food services sales by more than 1% over two consecutive months signals a strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS growth is positive, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
